tasks.spec:
You are a build worker producing a mechanical graph validator. OFFLINE: no network, no git, no MCP, no skills; write only inside your working directory.

INPUTS (read-only): /home/ankit114/repos/ringer/my-manifests/mk2-number-and-comeback/SPEC-v91.md section '## 4. Mechanical validator' is the AUTHORITATIVE requirements list — read the whole section and implement EVERY numbered assertion it contains (structure, per-delta checks D1-D4, classification-gate checks, text invariants). Reference graphs for field shapes: pathway-v86.json and pathway-v90.json in the same directory.

TASK: write ./check_v91_graph.py implementing the spec'd CLI exactly: python3 check_v91_graph.py --base <v86> --draft <candidate> --v88-ref <v90> --classification <json>. Exit 0 is the only PASS. Every failed assertion prints a line beginning with ' - ' explaining exactly what broke and where (node id, field). Collect ALL failures before exiting, do not stop at the first. No assertion may be a tautology. Also write ./stub-classification.json containing exactly {} for red-proof testing.

DESIGN NOTES: byte-identical comparisons via json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True) equality; the untouched-node set and untouched-edge set are enumerated in the spec; position/x/y/height/width ARE asserted on untouched nodes (mass drift is the regression fingerprint); every responsePathways destination must have a matching edge with agreeing label; classification file must cover every diff and use only the six bucket names, with OPEN items listed separately and causing a distinct printed warning line but not automatic failure (the spec defines which two OPEN items are pre-approved).

VERIFY before finishing: (1) python3 -m py_compile check_v91_graph.py passes; (2) running it with --draft pathway-v90.json (which is NOT a valid v91) and --classification stub-classification.json exits NONZERO and prints at least 5 distinct ' - ' failure lines including a node-count failure; (3) running with --draft pathway-v86.json also exits nonzero (missing the four deltas). Show both outputs in your final message.

Final message <=20 lines: assertion count implemented, the two red-proof outputs summarized, anything in spec section 4 you could not implement and why.
tasks.check: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m py_compile check_v91_graph.py && OUT=$(PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 check_v91_graph.py --base /home/ankit114/repos/ringer/my-manifests/mk2-number-and-comeback/pathway-v86.json --draft /home/ankit114/repos/ringer/my-manifests/mk2-number-and-comeback/pathway-v90.json --v88-ref /home/ankit114/repos/ringer/my-manifests/mk2-number-and-comeback/pathway-v90.json --classification stub-classification.json 2>&1); RC=$?; N=$(printf '%s' "$OUT" | grep -c -- ' - '); if [ $RC -ne 0 ] && [ $N -ge 5 ]; then echo "RED-PROOF OK: rc=$RC with $N printed reasons"; else echo "CHECK FAILED: rc=$RC reasons=$N"; printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | tail -15; exit 1; fi
tasks.verified: A validator implementing every SPEC-v91 section-4 assertion, proven RED against v90-as-draft with at least five printed reasons; the green proof comes when the real v91 draft is built against it.

ROLE: CONTRARIAN. Read /home/ankit114/repos/ringer/my-manifests/mk2-number-and-comeback/SPEC-v91.md in full, plus pathway-v86.json and pathway-v90.json for ground truth.
